title: Flattened characterization of the level matrix
statement: Let $w,r\in\mathbb{N}$, let $E$ be a relation on pairs of finite bit strings, and let $\tau:\mathbb{N}\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$ be a bit sequence. For every $j\in\mathbb{N}$, the recursively defined level-matrix condition at position $3w(j+1)$, with endpoint strings $u_j$ and $v_j$ given by the length-$w$ blocks of $\tau$ starting at $3wj+w$ and $3wj+2w$, respectively, holds if and only if either at some index $i<r$ the selector condition fails for the five blocks $u_{j+i},v_{j+i},z_{j+i+1},u_{j+i+1},v_{j+i+1}$, or $E(u_{j+r},v_{j+r})$ holds. Here $z_k$ is the length-$w$ block starting at $3wk$, and the selector condition means that either $(u_{j+i},v_{j+i})=(u_{j+i+1},z_{j+i+1})$ or $(u_{j+i+1},v_{j+i+1})=(z_{j+i+1},v_{j+i})$.
hypotheses_covered: $E$ is a relation on pairs of finite bit strings
$\tau$ is a bit sequence indexed by natural numbers
